# chrome.inkwork.studio

> A warm remote Chromium you drive with **one intent per call** — compact ref
> snapshots instead of screenshots, server-side batches instead of one call per
> click, and in-page reflexes that react in 4–16 ms so countdowns and
> fast-changing UI are usable by an agent.

Base URL: `https://chrome.inkwork.studio` (or `http://127.0.0.1:8787` locally).
Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $IW_TOKEN` on every `/api/*` and `/mcp` request.
The token is printed by the server and stored in `data/token`.

## The loop (three calls, not thirty)

1. **Open** — `POST /api/sessions` `{"name":"docs","url":"https://docs.google.com/…"}`
   → `{session:{id}}`. One warm Chromium context per session, isolated.
2. **Observe** — `POST /api/s/{id}/snap` `{"max":100}` → compact text tree with
   `@e12` refs, roles, values, bounds, and a `seq` number. ~3–10 ms engine time.
3. **Act** — `POST /api/s/{id}/act` with a whole batch. Returns the post-batch
   observation, so the next decision needs no extra call.

```json
POST /api/s/s_1/act
{"steps":[
  {"click":"@e4"},
  {"fill":{"ref":"@e12","text":"Ada Lovelace"}},
  {"fill":{"ref":"@e13","text":"ada@example.com"}},
  {"select":{"ref":"@e15","value":"engineer"}},
  {"click":{"text":"I agree"}},
  {"click":"Create account"}
]}
```

Set `"input":"dom"` to click in-page (roughly 3–10× faster than trusted CDP
input; works with most React apps). The default `"cdp"` sends real mouse events
for canvas, file pickers and flows that reject synthetic clicks.

`verify` defaults to `"change"`: it waits up to 300 ms for the control/URL/
title/dialog **signature** to change — a ticking clock alone does not count as
success. Use `"mutation"` for a raw DOM-mutation check, or `"none"` to skip
verification entirely when speed matters more. A failing step stops the batch
unless it sets `"optional": true`. Refs are stable for the life of the element and are refused
with `stale` if the element was replaced — a wrong-element click is never issued.

## Observing like a native, not like a screenshot tool

- `POST /api/s/{id}/pulse` → `{countdown:{est,rate,age,dir,...}, numbers, focus,
  dialogs, last_change_age_ms, seq, viewport}`. `est` is **seconds remaining
  extrapolated to read time** (`est * 1000` for ms) from a sample taken inside
  the page, so a 20 ms old sample of a 10 ms timer is corrected, not stale. The
  live console view lags the page; `pulse` is the ground truth. No screenshot
  (~45 ms) and no pixels to parse.
- `POST /api/s/{id}/wait` `{"text":"Saved","timeout_ms":8000}` → waits inside
  the page, in one request. Do not poll from the model.
- `POST /api/s/{id}/screenshot` → JPEG data URL. This is the slow path
  (~45 ms); use it for layout/canvas questions only.

## Reacting faster than a model: reflexes

`POST /api/s/{id}/reflex`

```json
{"until":"snap.countdown && snap.countdown.est < 1.5",
 "do":"iw.click('@e9')",
 "every_ms":8,
 "timeout_ms":10000}
```

`until` is a JS expression over `(iw, snap)`; `do` is a JS expression executed
the moment it becomes true. Both run **inside the page**, so the reaction is
measured in single-digit milliseconds. The response includes `reaction_ms` and
a sampled trace. This is the correct tool for Kahoot countdowns, quiz timers,
video cues, and any UI that changes faster than a model round trip.

## Code mode: `eval`

`POST /api/s/{id}/eval` `{"code":"return iw.snap({max:40})"}` runs JavaScript in
the page with the `iw` SDK. One call can loop, filter, aggregate and act over
hundreds of elements — the fastest path for scraping and repetitive flows.
Use `return` for the result; async is supported.

```js
// read every row of a table in one round trip
const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('table tr')].map(r => r.innerText);
return { rows: rows.slice(0, 20), n: rows.length };
```

### `iw` SDK (in-page)

| call | meaning |
|---|---|
| `iw.snap({max, scope})` | compact ref tree + `text` |
| `iw.pulse()` | timers, scores, focus, dialogs, mutation age |
| `iw.click(ref \| text \| {selector} \| {x,y})` | page-side click (instant, synthetic) |
| `iw.fill(ref, text)` | native setter / execCommand; React-safe |
| `iw.select(ref, value)` / `iw.check(ref, on)` | form controls |
| `iw.waitFor({text, selector, predicate, since, timeout_ms})` | in-page wait |
| `iw.reflex({until, do, every_ms, timeout_ms})` | in-page reflex |
| `iw.read(target?, max?)` / `iw.find(text)` | text extraction |
| `iw.sig()` | control/url/title/dialog signature (verification) |
| `iw.log(...)` | returns in the eval response `logs` |

`iw.click` is synthetic (fast, works for most apps). Use the declarative `act`
steps when you need trusted CDP mouse/keyboard events.

## Recipes (heuristic shortcuts)

`GET /api/recipes` lists them; `POST /api/s/{id}/recipe/quiz.state` etc.

- `quiz.state` → question, answer tiles with refs, countdown, score, phase.
- `quiz.answer` `{"index":1}` / `{"text":"Mars"}` → picks an answer.
- `kahoot.join` `{"pin":"123456","name":"agent"}` → opens kahoot.it, accepts
  cookies, enters the PIN and nickname. `dry_run:true` stops after the PIN.
- `doc.append` `{"text":"…"}` → appends to a contenteditable/Docs-style editor.
- `doc.read` → visible document text.

They are heuristics over generic quiz/doc UIs (tested against Kahoot-shaped and
Docs-shaped fixtures), not vendor integrations. Read the returned `evidence`.

## MCP

Add as a remote MCP server (streamable HTTP, stateless):

```json
{"mcpServers":{"chrome":{"type":"http","url":"https://chrome.inkwork.studio/mcp",
  "headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer $IW_TOKEN"}}}}
```

Tools: `chrome_sessions`, `chrome_open`, `chrome_snap`, `chrome_act`,
`chrome_eval`, `chrome_pulse`, `chrome_reflex`, `chrome_wait`, `chrome_close`.
Each tool call is one intent. Do not use one call per click.

## Latency budget (measured on the NAS, see /api/metrics)

| operation | p50 | notes |
|---|---|---|
| in-page eval | ~1 ms | CDP round trip |
| snapshot (small page) | ~3–8 ms | server-merged, frame-aware |
| batched act (8 steps) | ~40 ms | includes trusted input + verify |
| pulse | ~1–2 ms | no screenshot |
| screenshot | ~45 ms | avoid in the loop |
| reflex reaction | 4–16 ms | inside the page, no network |

## Limits and safety

- `IW_MAX_SESSIONS` (default 4) warm contexts; each is isolated (own cookies,
  storage, permissions). Sessions expire only when closed or the process stops.
- URLs are restricted to `http(s)` and `about:blank`; uploads must live under
  `data/uploads`.
- This is a browser-control service: the token is equivalent to control of the
  browser. Put it behind HTTPS + a long token (or Cloudflare Access) before
  exposing it. Do not run it on a shared host without a gate.
- `POST /api/s/{id}/eval` executes page JavaScript, not Node. The browser can
  still reach private-network URLs; treat it as a network foothold.

## Tabs and viewport

```
GET  /api/s/{id}/tabs                        -> [{id, url, title, active}]
POST /api/s/{id}/tabs {"action":"new","url":"https://…"}
POST /api/s/{id}/tabs {"action":"activate","id":"t2"}
POST /api/s/{id}/tabs {"action":"close","id":"t2"}
POST /api/s/{id}/viewport {"width":390,"height":844}   # render a mobile layout
```

`snap`, `act`, `eval` and `screenshot` always target the **active** tab.

## The human window

`/` is a plain browser UI (tabs, address bar, live view, touch on phones) for the
person watching. `/console` is the diagnostics view. Neither is required by an
agent; ignore both unless you are debugging visually.
